sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的每日新闻简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is them.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们。

sentences.en: Do you agree today that you were wrong to oppose busing in America then?
sentences.zh: 你今天是否承认，当时反对美国的校车接送政策是错误的？

sentences.en: Do you agree?
sentences.zh: 你承认吗？

sentences.en: I did not oppose busing in
sentences.zh: 我并没有反对美国的

sentences.en: America.
sentences.zh: 校车接送政策。

sentences.en: The first Democratic debate brought renewed attention to busing as a tool of school desegregation.
sentences.zh: 民主党首场辩论让校车接送政策作为学校废除种族隔离的工具再次受到关注。

sentences.en: My colleague, Nicole Hannah-Jones, on what the conversation since then has been missing.
sentences.zh: 我的同事妮可·汉娜-琼斯将探讨自那以来的对话中缺失了什么。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, July 18th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月18日，星期四。

sentences.en: Nicole, I want to start by going back a couple of weeks to the first
sentences.zh: 妮可，我想先回到几周前的首场

sentences.en: Democratic primary debate.
sentences.zh: 民主党初选辩论。

sentences.en: What's on your mind as that debate comes to an end?
sentences.zh: 那场辩论结束后，你有什么想法？

sentences.en: I'm just really surprised that Kamala Harris goes so directly at Joe Biden about the issue of busing and school segregation.
sentences.zh: 我真的很惊讶卡玛拉·哈里斯在校车接送和学校种族隔离问题上如此直接地针对乔·拜登。

sentences.en: It was very unexpected.
sentences.zh: 这非常出人意料。

sentences.en: And I'm kind of watching the conversation on Twitter, and almost universally, people were saying busing was a failed policy.
sentences.zh: 我在推特上关注了相关讨论，几乎所有人都在说校车接送是一项失败的政策。

sentences.en: You want to talk about busing?
sentences.zh: 你想谈谈校车接送吗？

sentences.en: I was up here in Boston.
sentences.zh: 我当时就在波士顿。

sentences.en: It was a failure.
sentences.zh: 那是一次失败。

sentences.en: He should have been against busing.
sentences.zh: 他本该反对校车接送的。

sentences.en: We should have been against busing.
sentences.zh: 我们本该反对校车接送的。

sentences.en: Bussing was super unpopular, and busing was a failure.
sentences.zh: 校车接送非常不受欢迎，而且是一项失败的政策。

sentences.en: People didn't like busing.
sentences.zh: 人们不喜欢校车接送。

sentences.en: Black people, white people, nobody liked busing.
sentences.zh: 黑人、白人，没人喜欢校车接送。

sentences.en: It wasn't the right solution.
sentences.zh: 那不是正确的解决方案。

sentences.en: And what did you make of that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有何看法？

sentences.en: Because I have to admit, my sense is that busing was something that failed to achieve its goals.
sentences.zh: 因为我必须承认，我的感觉是校车接送未能实现其目标。

sentences.en: It wasn't surprising to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说并不意外。

sentences.en: I've been writing a bus school segregation for more than 15 years, and this is a very common narrative.
sentences.zh: 我研究学校种族隔离问题已经超过15年了，这是一种非常普遍的叙事。

sentences.en: But that's actually not the truth.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And if you study the history of the policy, and if you study the results of the policy, where it was implemented intentionally, it actually was dramatically successful.
sentences.zh: 如果你研究这项政策的历史，研究它的实施结果，在那些有意识地实施该政策的地方，它实际上取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So let's go back to that history.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们回到那段历史。

sentences.en: Where, in your mind, does that start?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，这一切是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: I mean, to go back, you have to go back to the Supreme Court ruling in 1954 in the landmark Brown v.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，要追溯过去，必须回到1954年最高法院对具有里程碑意义的布朗诉

sentences.en: Board of Education ruling.
sentences.zh: 教育委员会案的裁决。

sentences.en: In a unanimous decision, the nine Supreme Court justices ruled racial segregation in publicly supported schools to be unconstitutional, declaring that it denied equal opportunity.
sentences.zh: 九位最高法院大法官一致裁定，公立学校的种族隔离违宪，并宣布这剥夺了平等机会。

sentences.en: I think we sometimes forget how radical of a ruling that was.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们有时会忘记那项裁决是多么激进。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, we are told by the Supreme Court that the whole basis for our society in the South has not only been wrong, but 100 percent wrong.
sentences.zh: 最高法院突然告诉我们，我们整个南方社会的基础不仅是错误的，而且是百分之百错误的。

sentences.en: That overnight, nine unelected judges who served for life decided that the racial caste system that had been accepted in law was no longer constitutional.
sentences.zh: 一夜之间，九位终身任职、未经选举的法官决定，法律所接受的种族等级制度不再符合宪法。

sentences.en: Southerners had wakened one morning to find themselves labeled villains living outside the law.
sentences.zh: 南方人一觉醒来，发现自己被贴上了生活在法律之外的恶棍标签。

sentences.en: And of course, there is resistance to the ruling.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们对这项裁决进行了抵制。

sentences.en: I draw the line in the dust and toss the gauntlet before the feet of tyranny, and I say segregation now, segregation tomorrow, and segregation forever.
sentences.zh: 我在尘土中划下界线，将挑战抛在暴政的脚下，我说：现在种族隔离，明天种族隔离，永远种族隔离。

sentences.en: And the resistance is very substantial.
sentences.zh: 这种抵制非常强烈。

sentences.en: Within the South, we must organize every county, every city, and every community.
sentences.zh: 在南方，我们必须组织每一个县、每一个城市和每一个社区。

sentences.en: A group of Southern senators, most of them Democrats, get together, and they decide that they are going to implement a policy of massive resistance.
sentences.zh: 一群南方参议员，其中大多数是民主党人，聚在一起，决定实施大规模抵制政策。

sentences.en: When groups can control the Supreme Court and control the president of the United States, I don't have to tell you that they must be reckoned with.
sentences.zh: 当某些群体能够控制最高法院和美国总统时，我不用说你也知道，他们是必须被重视的。

sentences.en: They just reject the Supreme Court's ruling.
sentences.zh: 他们直接拒绝了最高法院的裁决。

sentences.en: Outright.
sentences.zh: 彻底拒绝。

sentences.en: So they get together and they draft what's called the Southern Manifesto.
sentences.zh: 于是他们聚在一起，起草了所谓的《南方宣言》。

sentences.en: It was without legal force, but it dramatically proclaimed the determination to resist desegregation and express the South's anger at what it considered outside interference.
sentences.zh: 它虽然没有法律效力，但却大声疾呼要抵制废除种族隔离，并表达了南方对所谓外部干涉的愤怒。

sentences.en: Fully one-fifth of the men serving in Congress at that time, and they were all men, signed that Southern Manifesto.
sentences.zh: 当时在国会任职的议员中，足足有五分之一的人签署了这份《南方宣言》，而且他们全都是男性。

sentences.en: The court was saying, the way that you have lived, what the law has allowed, is actually not constitutional.
sentences.zh: 法院当时说，你们的生活方式以及法律所允许的一切，实际上是不符合宪法的。

sentences.en: And they were arguing, yes, it is, and the court does not have the right to say that it's not.
sentences.zh: 而他们则争辩说，不，这是合法的，法院无权说它不合法。

sentences.en: The resistance that follows that is, in many places, violent.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的抵制在许多地方是暴力的。

sentences.en: We want segregated schools at any coSt.
sentences.zh: 我们不惜一切代价想要种族隔离的学校。

sentences.en: And when I say any cost, I mean any coSt.
sentences.zh: 当我说是任何代价时，我是指任何代价。

sentences.en: Cost of life, if necessary.
sentences.zh: 如果有必要，包括生命的代价。

sentences.en: Just with a single Black child getting ready to integrate a school, we saw schools being bombed, buses being bombed.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为一个黑人孩子准备进入一所学校，我们就看到学校被炸，校车被炸。

sentences.en: We saw children being beaten, closing down schools.
sentences.zh: 我们看到孩子们被殴打，学校被迫关闭。

sentences.en: And rather than seeing the children of the white people of Georgia surrendered to the
sentences.zh: 与其看着佐治亚州白人的孩子向最高法院和亚特兰大报社投降，

sentences.en: Supreme Court and Atlanta newspapers, I would prefer abolishing public education forever and eternal.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿永远废除公共教育。

sentences.en: And did they close down schools?
sentences.zh: 他们真的关闭了学校吗？

sentences.en: Yes, in some places, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，在某些地方，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Kind of the most infamous place is Prince Edwards County in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 最臭名昭著的地方是弗吉尼亚州的爱德华王子县。

sentences.en: They closed down the schools in that county for five years.
sentences.zh: 他们在那个县关闭了学校五年。

sentences.en: For five years, there was no public school system in Prince Edwards County.
sentences.zh: 整整五年，爱德华王子县没有公立学校系统。

sentences.en: The white children got private vouchers that were paid with public tax dollars to attend private academies.
sentences.zh: 白人孩子获得了由公共税款支付的私人代金券，可以去私立学校上学。

sentences.en: And Black children got no schools whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 而黑人孩子则根本没有学校可去。

sentences.en: Because the schools had been closed.
sentences.zh: 因为学校已经被关闭了。

sentences.en: Because the schools had been closed and they were not given vouchers to attend private schools.
sentences.zh: 因为学校被关闭了，而且他们没有得到去私立学校上学的代金券。

sentences.en: That ends finally when the Supreme Court gets serious and orders the schools back open.
sentences.zh: 这种情况最终在最高法院认真起来并下令重新开放学校时才结束。

sentences.en: And that's the only reason public schools open back up in Prince Edwards County.
sentences.zh: 这就是爱德华王子县公立学校重新开放的唯一原因。

sentences.en: So these battles are very much out in the open in the South.
sentences.zh: 所以这些斗争在南方是非常公开的。

sentences.en: Politicians are saying we don't want to integrate.
sentences.zh: 政客们说我们不想融合。

sentences.en: And the government is saying that's too bad, but you have to.
sentences.zh: 而政府说那太遗憾了，但你们必须这样做。

sentences.en: What's happening at this time in the northern states?
sentences.zh: 当时北方各州发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, in the northern states, it's interesting because the northern white communities initially applaud the Brown v.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在北方各州，情况很有趣，因为北方的白人社区最初对布朗诉

sentences.en: Board of Education ruling.
sentences.zh: 教育委员会案的裁决表示赞赏。

sentences.en: The North has long liked to separate itself as not being racially backwards like the South.
sentences.zh: 北方长期以来喜欢将自己与南方区分开来，认为自己不像南方那样在种族问题上落后。

sentences.en: And so they saw the ruling as forcing the South to treat its black citizens like citizens.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们将这项裁决视为强迫南方像对待公民一样对待其黑人公民。

sentences.en: But that's because most white northern communities did not actually believe Brown v.
sentences.zh: 但这仅仅是因为大多数北方白人社区实际上并不认为布朗诉

sentences.en: Board of Education applied to them.
sentences.zh: 教育委员会案适用于他们自己。

sentences.en: They considered that Brown v.
sentences.zh: 他们认为布朗诉

sentences.en: Board was only about segregation that was explicitly written into the law.
sentences.zh: 教育委员会案仅涉及明确写入法律的种族隔离。

sentences.en: And of course, by the 1950s, segregation in the North was largely happening through other official policies,
sentences.zh: 当然，到了20世纪50年代，北方的种族隔离主要通过其他官方政策发生，

sentences.en: such as school boards that were gerrymandering attendance zones to maintain white and black schools, or housing policy that ensured that schools reflected residential segregation.
sentences.zh: 例如通过操纵学区划分来维持白人学校和黑人学校的学校董事会，或者确保学校反映居住隔离的住房政策。

sentences.en: So many folks in the North just didn't think it applied.
sentences.zh: 所以北方许多人根本不认为这适用于他们。

sentences.en: But black people thought differently.
sentences.zh: 但黑人的想法不同。

sentences.en: So black people see the Brown v.
sentences.zh: 所以黑人看到了布朗诉

sentences.en: Board of Education ruling and immediately begin to call out the hypocrisy of white northerners and say, have you been to the schools in our neighborhoods?
sentences.zh: 教育委员会案的裁决，并立即开始指出北方白人的虚伪，说：你们去过我们社区的学校吗？

sentences.en: Have you seen the schools in Chicago, in Detroit?
sentences.zh: 你们见过芝加哥、底特律的学校吗？

sentences.en: They looked and they are just as segregated as those in Mississippi and those in Alabama.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来和密西西比州和阿拉巴马州的学校一样，存在种族隔离。

sentences.en: And so they began to challenge and say that they believe they also had constitutional rights to integration under Brown v.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们开始挑战并表示，他们认为根据布朗诉

sentences.en: Board.
sentences.zh: 教育委员会案，他们也拥有融合的宪法权利。

sentences.en: Well, what does it actually look like in one of those northern cities like New York City, for example?
sentences.zh: 那么，在像纽约市这样的北方城市，实际情况是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: So New York City at that time is actually one of the most residentially segregated cities in the country.
sentences.zh: 当时的纽约市实际上是全国居住隔离最严重的城市之一。

sentences.en: The New York City School Board, at the behest of white parents, is gerrymandering attendance zones so that white kids can remain in white schools
sentences.zh: 纽约市教育委员会在白人家长的要求下，操纵学区划分，以便白人孩子可以留在白人学校，

sentences.en: and black kids will be funneled to black schools.
sentences.zh: 而黑人孩子则被输送到黑人学校。

sentences.en: And there is a distinct difference between the schools that black and white kids attend.
sentences.zh: 黑人孩子和白人孩子就读的学校之间存在明显的差异。

sentences.en: So the schools in New York City for black children are receiving sometimes half the funding of schools that white children attend to.
sentences.zh: 所以纽约市黑人孩子的学校获得的资金有时只有白人孩子学校的一半。

sentences.en: You're already starting to see the white population in New York City declining.
sentences.zh: 你已经开始看到纽约市的白人人口在减少。

sentences.en: So to keep schools white, you have to keep white schools partially empty.
sentences.zh: 所以为了保持学校的白人性质，你必须让白人学校保持部分空置。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the black population is rising.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，黑人人口在增加。

sentences.en: And so they are stuffing black kids into black schools.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把黑人孩子塞进黑人学校。

sentences.en: And some of the schools in black neighborhoods become so crowded that they begin to send black kids to schools in shifts.
sentences.zh: 黑人社区的一些学校变得非常拥挤，以至于他们开始分批次安排黑人孩子上学。

sentences.en: Even though there are empty white schools not far away.
sentences.zh: 尽管不远处就有空置的白人学校。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in some cases they're getting half the education of white kids.
sentences.zh: 所以在某些情况下，他们接受的教育只有白人孩子的一半。

sentences.en: And what activists in New York City are arguing is that the conditions that black children are facing in New York City
sentences.zh: 纽约市的活动人士认为，黑人孩子在纽约市面临的情况，

sentences.en: actually look very similar to the conditions that black children are facing in a place like Alabama.
sentences.zh: 实际上与黑人孩子在阿拉巴马州等地面临的情况非常相似。

sentences.en: And achievement tests are also reflecting that.
sentences.zh: 成绩测试也反映了这一点。

sentences.en: So black children's test scores in New York City are sometimes worse than test scores in parts of the South.
sentences.zh: 所以纽约市黑人孩子的考试成绩有时比南方部分地区的考试成绩还要差。

sentences.en: And when does this all come to a head?
sentences.zh: 这一切什么时候达到顶峰？

sentences.en: So it comes to a head in 1964.
sentences.zh: 这在1964年达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: The black and Puerto Rican communities in New York City have had enough.
sentences.zh: 纽约市的黑人和波多黎各社区已经忍无可忍了。

sentences.en: And they stage, the children stage a walkout.
sentences.zh: 于是他们组织了罢课，孩子们组织了罢课。

sentences.en: They do a one-day boycott where about 460,000 black and Puerto Rican students do not show up to school that day.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了一天的抵制，大约46万名黑人和波多黎各学生那天没有去学校。

sentences.en: All we want is equal education.
sentences.zh: 我们想要的只是平等的教育。

sentences.en: That's all.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: Equal education.
sentences.zh: 平等的教育。

sentences.en: It's actually the largest demonstration for civil rights in the history of the United States.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是美国历史上规模最大的民权示威活动。

sentences.en: But one almost no one has heard of.
sentences.zh: 但几乎没人听说过。

sentences.en: And what comes of that day of protest in New York?
sentences.zh: 纽约那天的抗议活动结果如何？

sentences.en: It's kind of amazing the backlash that those activists and those students faced for daring just not to show up for a day.
sentences.zh: 那些活动人士和学生仅仅因为敢于一天不去上学而面临的强烈反对，真是令人惊讶。

sentences.en: So the editorial board of the New York Times basically calls them, you know, a bunch of scofflaws, truants who are skipping school by adult sanction.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的编辑委员会基本上称他们为一群蔑视法律的人，是在成年人的怂恿下逃学的旷课者。

sentences.en: And a lot of the white supporters get very angry.
sentences.zh: 许多白人支持者也非常愤怒。

sentences.en: They feel like the black and Puerto Rican communities are pushing too hard, that this was a sign of them getting out of control and not being practical.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得黑人和波多黎各社区做得太过分了，认为这是他们失控且不切实际的迹象。

sentences.en: The New York City Public Schools, however, responds by deciding to implement a very small,
sentences.zh: 然而，纽约市公立学校的回应是决定实施一个非常小、

sentences.en: very limited busing program for desegregation between 30 black and Puerto Rican schools and 30 white schools.
sentences.zh: 非常有限的校车接送计划，在30所黑人和波多黎各学校与30所白人学校之间进行废除种族隔离。

sentences.en: And how does that go?
sentences.zh: 结果如何？

sentences.en: All hell breaks loose.
sentences.zh: 一片混乱。

sentences.en: The white parents do not respond well to this idea of even a very minor busing plan.
sentences.zh: 白人家长对这种即使是非常微小的校车接送计划的想法反应并不好。

sentences.en: And they come together and stage a protest of their own.
sentences.zh: 他们聚在一起，组织了自己的抗议活动。

sentences.en: They do a march.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了一次游行。

sentences.en: And what's fascinating about this is they, at this time, had studied what wasn't working with white resistance in the South.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他们当时研究了南方白人抵制运动中哪些方法行不通。

sentences.en: And they decide that they are actually going to model their protest after the civil rights movement and the tactics of the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 他们决定实际上要以民权运动及其策略为蓝本进行抗议。

sentences.en: Well, we feel that we can prove as much as our opponents who use the same tactics.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们觉得我们可以像我们的对手一样证明这一点，他们也使用同样的策略。

sentences.en: We feel that we have as much right as they were just to, these are our civil rights and we're taking advantage of them.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得我们和他们一样有权利，这些是我们的民权，我们正在利用它们。

sentences.en: It's very smart.
sentences.zh: 这非常聪明。

sentences.en: Because what they're realizing is it will not play well on media if they are announcing that they are protesting black children coming into their schools or their children going into black schools.
sentences.zh: 因为他们意识到，如果公开宣称抗议黑人儿童进入他们的学校，或者抗议自己的孩子进入黑人学校，这在媒体上会产生负面影响。

sentences.en: So they picked this race-neutral term of busing and they're saying, we have a right for our children to go to neighborhood schools.
sentences.zh: 于是他们选择了“校车接送”这个种族中立的词汇，并声称：我们有权让孩子就近上学。

sentences.en: This is our civil right.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的公民权利。

sentences.en: You see, then, white communities across the country, particularly in the Northeast and the Midwest, also saying, this is how we are going to proteSt.
sentences.zh: 于是你看到，全国各地的白人社区，尤其是东北部和中西部地区，也纷纷表示：这就是我们要抗议的方式。

sentences.en: Don't a bus when I have a school right across the street from where they should go.
sentences.zh: 当街对面就有学校时，凭什么要我坐校车？

sentences.en: It's a playbook that becomes adopted in white communities all across the Midwest and the NortheaSt.
sentences.zh: 这套策略后来被中西部和东北部各地的白人社区所采纳。

sentences.en: Just because I'm white doesn't mean that the 14th Amendment doesn't, doesn't be part of me either.
sentences.zh: 我身为白人，并不意味着第十四修正案就不适用于我。

sentences.en: I am white and I want my rights.
sentences.zh: 我是白人，我也想要我的权利。

sentences.en: Protesters against busing, quote unquote, stage a march on Washington.
sentences.zh: 所谓的“反校车接送”抗议者在华盛顿举行了游行。

sentences.en: A group of mothers from Michigan today completed a 44-day walk to Washington to protest school busing.
sentences.zh: 今天，一群来自密歇根州的母亲完成了为期44天的徒步进京之旅，以抗议学校校车接送政策。

sentences.en: Which, of course, follows the march on Washington that Dr. King had.
sentences.zh: 当然，这紧随马丁·路德·金博士当年的华盛顿大游行之后。

sentences.en: We've labored long and we've been through a great deal of pain.
sentences.zh: 我们辛勤劳作了很久，也经历了巨大的痛苦。

sentences.en: But it's worth it because we have given birth now to the rekindling of the government, of the people, by the people and for the people.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都是值得的，因为我们现在促成了政府的重塑，实现了民有、民治、民享。

sentences.en: Look, you're here.
sentences.zh: 看，你到了。

sentences.en: So it becomes very, very successful.
sentences.zh: 所以它变得非常、非常成功。

sentences.en: So their explicit argument is mostly about convenience.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们明确提出的论点大多是关于便利性。

sentences.en: We're not racist, but this is inconvenient and it's wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们不是种族主义者，但这很不方便，而且是错误的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The problem is when busing is being ordered in the North, when black kids are being bused into white neighborhoods, which means white kids are still in their neighborhood schools,
sentences.zh: 问题在于，当北方下令实行校车接送，即黑人孩子被送往白人社区的学校，而白人孩子仍留在本社区学校时，

sentences.en: those black kids are being met with violence.
sentences.zh: 那些黑人孩子却遭到了暴力对待。

sentences.en: I think that makes it clear that it was not just about wanting your kids to stay close to home.
sentences.zh: 我认为这清楚地表明，这不仅仅是关于想让孩子留在离家近的地方。

sentences.en: It was really about not wanting your kids to be in school with large numbers of black kids.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是不想让自己的孩子与大量黑人孩子一起上学。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court addresses this in 1971 when it takes up busing for the first time in a case known as Swan versus Mecklenburg County.
sentences.zh: 最高法院在1971年处理“斯旺诉梅克伦堡县案”时首次讨论了校车接送问题。

sentences.en: And in that case, the court upholds busing as a tool for desegregation.
sentences.zh: 在该案中，法院支持将校车接送作为废除种族隔离的工具。

sentences.en: And it says that, yes, you should be able to attend your neighborhood school.
sentences.zh: 法院表示，是的，你应该能够就近上学。

sentences.en: But absent a constitutional violation, there would be no basis for judicially ordering assignment of students on a racial basis.
sentences.zh: 但如果没有违反宪法，就没有理由通过司法手段强制按种族分配学生。

sentences.en: All things being equal, with no history of discrimination, it might well be desirable to assign pupils to schools nearest their homes.
sentences.zh: 在一切条件相同、且没有歧视历史的情况下，按离家最近的原则分配学生或许是可取的。

sentences.en: But all things are not equal in a system that has been deliberately constructed and maintained to enforce racial segregation.
sentences.zh: 但在一个为了强制实行种族隔离而蓄意构建和维持的系统中，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: This is like one of my favorite passages of all the rulings on school segregation that the court made.
sentences.zh: 这是法院在学校种族隔离裁决中我最喜欢的段落之一。

sentences.en: Because it's so rare that you see the Supreme Court so starkly laying out that the segregation we see was intentional.
sentences.zh: 因为最高法院如此直白地指出我们所见的种族隔离是蓄意的，这种情况非常罕见。

sentences.en: And we have to be just as intentional about undoing the segregation.
sentences.zh: 我们必须同样蓄意地去消除这种隔离。

sentences.en: You have to move bodies around.
sentences.zh: 你必须进行人员调动。

sentences.en: You actually have to undo what they call the dual system of black schools and white schools.
sentences.zh: 你实际上必须废除他们所谓的黑人学校和白人学校的双重体系。

sentences.en: Integration means one can look across the school system and not see black schools or white schools, but simply schools.
sentences.zh: 融合意味着人们审视整个学校系统时，看到的不再是黑人学校或白人学校，而仅仅是学校。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Okay, so despite these anti-busing movements, busing is the law of the land.
sentences.zh: 好的，尽管有这些反校车运动，但校车接送已是国家法律。

sentences.en: Take us back to the South.
sentences.zh: 带我们回到南方看看。

sentences.en: What are the results of this policy there?
sentences.zh: 那里的政策结果如何？

sentences.en: It's kind of remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这相当引人注目。

sentences.en: I think it's been a beneficial experience for all of them, without exception.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对他们所有人来说都是一次有益的经历，无一例外。

sentences.en: You see the South going from, in 1964, a full decade after Brown, just 2% of black children were attending a desegregated school.
sentences.zh: 你看，在1964年，即《布朗诉教育委员会案》判决十年后，南方只有2%的黑人儿童在非种族隔离学校上学。

sentences.en: Within 8 years, you had the majority of black children attending desegregated schools.
sentences.zh: 八年之内，大多数黑人儿童都在非种族隔离学校上学了。

sentences.en: Furthermore, they had become much more sensitive and much more capable academically.
sentences.zh: 此外，他们在学术上也变得更加敏感和更有能力。

sentences.en: So very, very quickly, the dominoes fall in the South when the South is being blanketed with desegregation orders.
sentences.zh: 所以，当南方被废除种族隔离令覆盖时，多米诺骨牌很快就倒下了。

sentences.en: And when the court says you actually have to move bodies, the South moves bodies.
sentences.zh: 当法院说你确实需要调动人员时，南方就调动了人员。

sentences.en: And what I've generally seen is that they have left one secluded part of the city and become a part of this nation.
sentences.zh: 我普遍看到的是，他们离开了城市中一个与世隔绝的部分，成为了这个国家的一部分。

sentences.en: And black and white kids are attending schools together.
sentences.zh: 黑人和白人孩子在一起上学。

sentences.en: Last year when I rode the bus well, I thought people were going to make fun of me.
sentences.zh: 去年我坐校车时，嗯，我以为人们会嘲笑我。

sentences.en: But it wasn't bad at all.
sentences.zh: 但一点也不糟糕。

sentences.en: And now I ride the bus every day.
sentences.zh: 现在我每天都坐校车。

sentences.en: The South goes from complete apartheid to being the most integrated region of the country in a matter of 10 years.
sentences.zh: 在短短10年内，南方从完全的种族隔离变成了全国融合程度最高的地区。

sentences.en: If this isn't a valuable thing for a child, and if this isn't part of a child's education, and a part of his becoming a citizen, then I don't really know what is.
sentences.zh: 如果这对孩子来说不是一件有价值的事，如果这不是孩子教育的一部分，也不是他成为公民过程的一部分，那我真不知道什么是了。

sentences.en: Busing can work, but it has to work under certain conditions.
sentences.zh: 校车接送可以奏效，但必须在特定条件下才能奏效。

sentences.en: It's a very brief moment in time where all three branches of the federal government actually work together to secure the civil rights of black children in the South.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常短暂的时刻，联邦政府的三个分支机构实际上共同努力，保障了南方黑人儿童的公民权利。

sentences.en: And when we put our minds to it and we decided that this is what we were going to do, it actually was extremely effective.
sentences.zh: 当我们下定决心，决定这就是我们要做的时，它实际上非常有效。

sentences.en: And amazingly, most white people in the South, once they were forced to, simply dealt with it.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，大多数南方的白人一旦被迫接受，也就顺其自然了。

sentences.en: And what about the North?
sentences.zh: 那么北方呢？

sentences.en: So the North is always a different story.
sentences.zh: 北方的情况总是不同。

sentences.en: What happens in the North is judges are also ordering busing for desegregation.
sentences.zh: 在北方，法官们也在下令进行废除种族隔离的校车接送。

sentences.en: But the North is geographically organized in a very different way than the South.
sentences.zh: 但北方的地理组织方式与南方截然不同。

sentences.en: The South was organized around these countywide districts because it was simply much more agrarian.
sentences.zh: 南方围绕着县级学区组织，因为那里主要是农业地区。

sentences.en: And you didn't have multiple large population centers,
sentences.zh: 而且没有多个大型人口中心，

sentences.en: so they just made one big school district that would cover usually a single big city and then all of its suburbs and its rural areas.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是建立了一个覆盖通常是一个大城市及其所有郊区和农村地区的大型学区。

sentences.en: The North, of course, was much more densely populated and developed in a very different way.
sentences.zh: 当然，北方人口密度更高，发展方式也大不相同。

sentences.en: So you had multiple school districts in a single county, which meant if you were going to get desegregation, you would have to cover every single school district in that county.
sentences.zh: 因此，一个县里有多个学区，这意味着如果你要实现种族融合，就必须覆盖该县的每一个学区。

sentences.en: And most times you would have a city and a judge would say this city schools are very segregated and it would order busing within that city.
sentences.zh: 大多数情况下，城市里会有法官说这个城市的学校种族隔离非常严重，并下令在该市内进行校车接送。

sentences.en: And then white people would just leave.
sentences.zh: 然后白人就会直接搬走。

sentences.en: Why wouldn't judges in the North order these metropolitan-style desegregations like we saw in the South and just disregard these broken-up school districts?
sentences.zh: 为什么北方的法官不效仿南方，下令进行这种大都市式的种族融合，直接无视这些支离破碎的学区呢？

sentences.en: Well, a judge in the North did attempt to do that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，北方的确有一位法官尝试过这样做。

sentences.en: So in the late 1960s, black parents in Detroit filed a lawsuit and they sued the city of Detroit for unconstitutionally segregating their kids.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代末，底特律的黑人父母提起诉讼，控告底特律市违宪地隔离了他们的孩子。

sentences.en: The case lands in the court of Judge Roth and he orders a metropolitan desegregation order, a busing plan that would bus white kids from the suburbs into the black city of Detroit.
sentences.zh: 案件落到了罗斯法官手中，他下达了一项大都市种族融合令，即一项校车接送计划，将白人孩子从郊区送往黑人聚居的底特律市。

sentences.en: And he orders that because he becomes convinced by the case that the NAACP puts on that housing segregation was making it impossible to integrate black kids,
sentences.zh: 他之所以下达该命令，是因为全国有色人种协进会（NAACP）提供的证据让他确信，住房隔离使得黑人孩子无法融入，

sentences.en: but also that that housing segregation was also intentional and therefore unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 而且这种住房隔离也是蓄意的，因此是违宪的。

sentences.en: So he orders this plan and that plan is struck down by the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 于是他下达了该计划，但该计划被最高法院驳回了。

sentences.en: To approve the remedy ordered by the court in these circumstances would impose on the 53 outlying districts, not shown to have committed any constitutional violation,
sentences.zh: 在这些情况下批准法院下达的补救措施，将强加给53个外围学区，而这些学区并未被证明犯有任何违宪行为，

sentences.en: a wholly impermissible remedy.
sentences.zh: 这是一种完全不可接受的补救措施。

sentences.en: It says that you cannot bus students across school district lines for integration unless you show that every one of those white suburbs had discriminated against black students too.
sentences.zh: 法院称，除非你能证明每一个白人郊区也歧视了黑人学生，否则不能为了融合而跨学区接送学生。

sentences.en: It is clear that the case was decided before these 53 districts were given any chance to show that they had committed no violations of anyone's constitutional rights.
sentences.zh: 很明显，该案在这些53个学区有机会证明他们没有侵犯任何人宪法权利之前就已经做出了裁决。

sentences.en: But that, of course, is very impossible because if you are a white suburb that did not allow black people to settle there,
sentences.zh: 但这当然是不可能的，因为如果你是一个不允许黑人定居的白人郊区，

sentences.en: there's no record that you discriminated against black students.
sentences.zh: 就没有你歧视黑人学生的记录。

sentences.en: And it also sends a very powerful message to white people in the north that if you want to avoid integration,
sentences.zh: 这也向北方的白人传递了一个非常强烈的信号：如果你想避免种族融合，

sentences.en: all you have to do is move a couple miles up the road to an all-white community with its all-white schools.
sentences.zh: 你所要做的就是搬到几英里外一个全白人的社区，那里有全白人的学校。

sentences.en: Because the busing will not require you to leave.
sentences.zh: 因为校车接送不会要求你离开。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The busing will not penetrate that invisible municipal line.
sentences.zh: 校车接送不会穿透那条无形的市政界线。

sentences.en: So a lot of times we hear that busing is to blame for white flight.
sentences.zh: 所以我们经常听到人们把“白人大逃亡”归咎于校车接送。

sentences.en: I would argue really, though, it's that ruling that allows white families to know we can just move and we can avoid this, which you could not do in the south,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，真正让白人家庭知道“我们可以搬走来避免这种情况”（这在南方是做不到的）的，是那项裁决，

sentences.en: that really accelerates white flight.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正加速“白人大逃亡”的原因。

sentences.en: The court is largely responsible for that.
sentences.zh: 法院对此负有很大责任。

sentences.en: And we do see larger numbers of white people leaving cities after that ruling.
sentences.zh: 在那项裁决之后，我们确实看到更多的白人离开了城市。

sentences.en: So in this case, busing within a district didn't work.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个案例中，学区内的校车接送并没有奏效。

sentences.en: But the kind of busing that could have been effective, that could have worked, was essentially made impossible.
sentences.zh: 但那种本可能有效、本可能奏效的校车接送，基本上被变得不可能了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And that's what you see then occurring all across the Northeast and the Midwest, where judges are finding that black students' rights have been violated,
sentences.zh: 这就是你在整个东北部和中西部看到的情况，法官们发现黑人学生的权利受到了侵犯，

sentences.en: but there's no remedy because there's no white kids left in the district and you can't bus out to the suburbs where all the white kids are.
sentences.zh: 但却没有补救措施，因为学区里已经没有白人孩子了，而且你也不能把他们送到白人孩子所在的郊区去。

sentences.en: So with that in mind, I wonder if you could take us through the next decade or so of busing.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这一点，我想请你带我们回顾一下接下来十年的校车接送历程。

sentences.en: What happens to not just make it less effective, but to actually put an end to it?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致它不仅效果变差，甚至最终走向终结？

sentences.en: So there's two stories that are happening at the same time.
sentences.zh: 当时有两个故事在同时发生。

sentences.en: In the north, there's no real large-scale efforts to desegregate after that.
sentences.zh: 在北方，此后没有真正的大规模废除种族隔离的努力。

sentences.en: In the south, you see that desegregation is happening and it ends up peaking in 1988.
sentences.zh: 在南方，你可以看到种族融合正在发生，并最终在1988年达到顶峰。

sentences.en: So what does that look like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么样的？

sentences.en: What does it look like at its best?
sentences.zh: 它在最好的状态下是什么样的？

sentences.en: So after, you know, 20 years of really trying, by 1988, almost half of black kids are attending majority white schools.
sentences.zh: 在经过20年的真正努力后，到1988年，近一半的黑人孩子在以白人为主的学校上学。

sentences.en: But that means that even at the peak of desegregation in this country, most black kids were still not in majority white schools.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着，即使在这个国家种族融合的巅峰时期，大多数黑人孩子仍然不在以白人为主的学校上学。

sentences.en: That was the best the country could do.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个国家能做到的最好程度了。

sentences.en: That was the best the country did do.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个国家确实做到的最好程度。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And you said that 1988 was a peak.
sentences.zh: 你说1988年是一个巅峰。

sentences.en: What happened after 1988?
sentences.zh: 1988年之后发生了什么？

sentences.en: Reagan gets elected and he wants to try to close out these court orders.
sentences.zh: 里根当选，他想设法结束这些法院命令。

sentences.en: So he turns his Justice Department to try to end court orders,
sentences.zh: 于是他让司法部试图结束法院命令，

sentences.en: where before the Justice Department was fighting on behalf of black students and civil rights groups to expand integration.
sentences.zh: 而在此之前，司法部一直代表黑人学生和民权组织争取扩大融合。

sentences.en: Now it's siding with school boards to close these orders out.
sentences.zh: 现在它站在学校董事会一边，试图结束这些命令。

sentences.en: So you see a wave of school desegregation orders being ended in the south.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到南方掀起了一波结束学校废除种族隔离令的浪潮。

sentences.en: And once those orders are ended, school districts can pretty much do anything to resegregate schools as long as they don't explicitly do it for racist reasons.
sentences.zh: 一旦这些命令结束，学区几乎可以采取任何手段让学校重新隔离，只要他们不是明确出于种族主义原因这样做。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Nicole, which part of this history do you think is most overlooked when people say things as they did after the debate, that busing failed?
sentences.zh: 妮可，当人们像辩论后那样说“校车接送失败了”时，你认为这段历史中哪一部分最被忽视？

sentences.en: I think there are two things that are really overlooked.
sentences.zh: 我认为有两件事被严重忽视了。

sentences.en: One, in order to argue that busing failed, you have to ignore the entire region of the south, which is where half of black Americans live,
sentences.zh: 第一，为了证明校车接送失败，你必须忽略整个南方地区，那里居住着一半的美国黑人，

sentences.en: because it was tremendously successful in the south.
sentences.zh: 因为校车接送在南方取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: And the other thing that you have to look at is this belief that busing was not actually good for black kids.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是你必须审视这种观点，即认为校车接送对黑人孩子实际上没有好处。

sentences.en: And as someone who was bused myself, I would never argue that it wasn't difficult.
sentences.zh: 作为一个曾经坐过校车的人，我绝不会说这不困难。

sentences.en: But strictly in terms of did busing break up racial caste in this country?
sentences.zh: 但严格来说，校车接送是否打破了这个国家的种族等级制度？

sentences.en: And the answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: That black kids who got access to desegregated schools not only did it close or help narrow the racial achievement gap, but also changed the trajectory of their lives.
sentences.zh: 那些有机会进入非种族隔离学校的黑人孩子，不仅缩小了种族成就差距，还改变了他们的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: They were less likely to live in poverty.
sentences.zh: 他们生活在贫困中的可能性降低了。

sentences.en: They were more likely to graduate from college.
sentences.zh: 他们大学毕业的可能性更高了。

sentences.en: They earned more money as adults.
sentences.zh: 他们成年后赚的钱更多了。

sentences.en: They were less likely to be involved in the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 他们卷入刑事司法系统的可能性降低了。

sentences.en: And they even were healthier and lived longer.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至更健康，寿命更长。

sentences.en: That's really what desegregation was designed to do.
sentences.zh: 这才是废除种族隔离的真正目的。

sentences.en: And that's how desegregation worked in the places where we actually tried.
sentences.zh: 这就是废除种族隔离在我们真正尝试过的地方所起的作用。

sentences.en: And why is that, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: The evidence is actually very clear on this.
sentences.zh: 证据其实非常清楚。

sentences.en: And I want to make sure that no one who listens to this takes away the message that something about sitting next to white kids makes black kids smart.
sentences.zh: 我想确保听众不会得出“坐在白人孩子旁边就能让黑人孩子变聪明”这样的结论。

sentences.en: But what sitting next to white kids does for black kids is it ensures they get the education that we have always reserved for white kids in this country.
sentences.zh: 但坐在白人孩子旁边能为黑人孩子做的是，确保他们获得我们在这个国家一直为白人孩子保留的教育资源。

sentences.en: If they want to get the same resources as white kids, unfortunately, they have to be in the same classrooms as white kids.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想获得与白人孩子相同的资源，不幸的是，他们必须和白人孩子在同一个教室里。

sentences.en: And I think one of the most poignant examples of this is a story that black people at one of the prominent black high schools in Charlotte tell the day they knew the integration was coming to their school,
sentences.zh: 我认为最深刻的例子之一是夏洛特一所著名黑人高中的黑人学生讲述的故事，那天他们知道融合即将到来，

sentences.en: which is a crew of maintenance people arrive at the high school in Charlotte, and they fix that school up.
sentences.zh: 一群维修人员来到夏洛特的高中，把学校修缮了一番。

sentences.en: And they put the things in the lab that were supposed to be there and the new textbooks in the school.
sentences.zh: 他们把实验室里本该有的东西放了进去，还给学校换上了新课本。

sentences.en: And that's how they knew the integration was coming.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们知道融合即将到来的方式。

sentences.en: Because suddenly, when white kids were going to be there, these facilities were not good enough anymore, even though they had been just fine for the black kids attending there.
sentences.zh: 因为突然之间，当白人孩子要来这里时，这些设施就不再“足够好”了，尽管对于在那里上学的黑人孩子来说，它们一直都很好。

sentences.en: That is unfortunately the way that race has always worked in this country, is we have never disentangled race from resources.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这就是种族问题在这个国家一直运作的方式，我们从未将种族与资源剥离开来。

sentences.en: And we've never shown that we believe that black kids are deserving of the same resources as white kids.
sentences.zh: 我们也从未表现出我们相信黑人孩子值得拥有与白人孩子相同的资源。

sentences.en: I would argue that when you look at all the other ways we could have attempted to integrate our schools, busing was actually the most effective tool.
sentences.zh: 我认为，当你审视我们本可以尝试融合学校的所有其他方式时，校车接送实际上是最有效的工具。

sentences.en: And it was the most effective because it was the most immediate.
sentences.zh: 它是最有效的，因为它最直接。

sentences.en: Everything else that we could do and that we should do, integrate our housing, build new schools in areas that allow them to be more easily integrated,
sentences.zh: 我们能做且应该做的其他所有事情，比如融合住房、在更容易融合的地区建设新学校，

sentences.en: all of these things would have taken a very long time, decades even.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都需要很长时间，甚至几十年。

sentences.en: But busing could happen tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 但校车接送明天就能实现。

sentences.en: And I think it was because it was so immediate and because it was so effective that that's why we fought against it so hard.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是因为它如此直接且有效，我们才如此强烈地反对它。

sentences.en: Because we really didn't want to desegregate our schools.
sentences.zh: 因为我们真的不想让学校废除种族隔离。

sentences.en: We just wanted to pretend that we wanted to.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想假装我们想这样做。

sentences.en: We killed busing because it worked too well.
sentences.zh: 我们废除了校车接送计划，因为它太有效了。

sentences.en: Yes, that's what I would argue.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是我的观点。

sentences.en: Busing did not fail.
sentences.zh: 校车接送计划并没有失败。

sentences.en: We failed.
sentences.zh: 是我们失败了。

sentences.en: Nicole, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 妮可，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: I seek recognition to give notice of my intent to raise a question of the privileges of the House.
sentences.zh: 我请求发言，以告知我打算提出关于众议院特权的问题。

sentences.en: The form of the resolution is as follows.
sentences.zh: 决议的形式如下。

sentences.en: Impeaching Donald John Trump, president of the United States, of high misdemeanors.
sentences.zh: 弹劾美利坚合众国总统唐纳德·约翰·特朗普，因其犯有严重不当行为。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the House of Representatives blocked the first attempt to impeach President Trump since the Democrats took control of the House in January.
sentences.zh: 周三，众议院阻止了自民主党一月份控制众议院以来首次弹劾特朗普总统的尝试。

sentences.en: Resolved that Donald John Trump, president of the United States, is unfit to be president.
sentences.zh: 决议指出，美利坚合众国总统唐纳德·约翰·特朗普不适合担任总统。

sentences.en: Unfit to represent the American values of decency and morality, respectability and civility, honesty and propriety, reputability and integrity.
sentences.zh: 不适合代表美国关于体面与道德、尊严与文明、诚实与礼仪、声誉与正直的价值观。

sentences.en: The resolution to impeach, a response to the president's attacks on four Democratic congresswomen, was introduced by Representative Al Green, a Democrat from Texas,
sentences.zh: 这项弹劾决议是对总统攻击四位民主党女议员的回应，由来自德克萨斯州的民主党众议员阿尔·格林提出，

sentences.en: but was opposed by the majority of his fellow Democrats, including House Speaker Nancy Pelosi.
sentences.zh: 但遭到了包括众议院议长南希·佩洛西在内的大多数民主党同僚的反对。

sentences.en: With all the respect in the world for Mr. Green, we have six committees that are working on following the facts
sentences.zh: 我对格林先生怀有万分敬意，但我们有六个委员会正在致力于追查事实，

sentences.en: in terms of any abuse of power, obstruction of justice and the rest that the president may have engaged in.
sentences.zh: 针对总统可能涉及的任何滥用权力、妨碍司法以及其他行为。

sentences.en: That is the serious path that we are on.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们正在走的严肃道路。

sentences.en: Not that Mr. Green is not serious, but we'll deal with that on the floor.
sentences.zh: 并不是说格林先生不严肃，但我们会在议会大厅处理这个问题。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》节目。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你获取播客的任何地方收听。
